title: Anyone with published/successful ai assisted games ?
author: RewardNarrow

comments.author: Individual-Bet-5784
comments.body: What’s up? My game is fully made with ai, code and designs just be being the director,tester and my creativity

comments.author: Shalke97
comments.body: Yeah. I Sold around 1100 Copys so far, 2 months since Release and 87% Positive Reviews. Most of the negative reviews we're based on early EA Bugs i had to fix. "Grim Reach Idle"

replies.author: Shalke97
replies.body: Around 3,5k net. I'm selling my Game for 4,99 when its not on sale.

comments.author: West_Satisfaction299
comments.body: Not successful in terms of sales so far but it released, slowly getting press outreach week by week. Just got my second mention this week by a blog in Brazil. Total social following just under 200 followers across 3 platforms.

replies.author: derAres
replies.body: May I ask why you do social stuff?

replies.author: West_Satisfaction299
replies.body: It's led to some great discovery so far and it helps when I am pitching my game to blogs/magazines/influencers. I also used to be a social media manager 😄

replies.author: derAres
replies.body: Thanks... so You get strangers to follow your game on social media successfully? Or is this more a „I managed to get 200 people that I already know to follow“ kind of thing? I do seriously doubt that cost/benefit makes sense for an indie dev. Why would the algorhythm suggest some indie game to people you don’t already know?

comments.author: Kitchen-Many-8466
comments.body: where does it actually plug in for you? like is it the "generate 500 sprites and pick 5" thing or more like the "i'm iterating on a mechanic 10x faster" thing? those feel like completely different experiences
